subject: Action needed: service reachability disruption — US-East + EU-Central (opt-in fallback instructions)
messages:
From: Sophie Zhang <sophie@acmeanalytics.com>

Date: 2026-04-18T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in 503s for US-East + EU-Central — are there opt-in fallbacks?

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a spike in 503/connection timeouts for requests served from US-East and EU-Central around 08:15 PT. Our app is reporting failed generations and the team is getting alerts. Can you confirm if this is on your side or a provider peering issue?

We have attached a short log excerpt (acme_error_log_0418.txt). Is there a way for you to temporarily route our traffic to another region (APAC) while you investigate? We can also flip a client-side header if that helps — what would you recommend?

Sophie

Hi Sophie — thanks for the log excerpt and the heads-up. We're seeing elevated error rates for US-East and EU-Central in our telemetry (matching the timestamp you sent).

Immediate plan:
- I'm escalating to infra (cc'd Karthik) to confirm cause.
- We can enable an opt-in client-side preference that prefers APAC nodes for your account while we remediate. That requires a single header (X-Redwood-Region: apac) or a per-deployment config change; I'll include exact instructions below.
- We'll keep you informed every 30–45 minutes until this is resolved.

For now please:
1) If you can, add the header X-Redwood-Region: apac to a small percentage (5–10%) of traffic to validate behavior.
2) Share any additional logs if you see expanded failure patterns.

I'll follow up shortly with the infra assessment and a one-page checklist (attaching redwood-optin-checklist-20260418.pdf).

— Rishi

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-04-18T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Spike in 503s for US-East + EU-Central — are there opt-in fallbacks?

Quick triage notes (infra):
- Root cause (initial): inter-provider peering flap impacting two POPs used heavily by our US-East and EU-Central placements. Packet loss led to degraded connections and upstream timeouts for a subset of nodes.
- Mitigations performed: drained affected instances, bumped fallback weights toward apac-pool, increased kv-cache TTLs to reduce token regen calls, and applied a temporary connection retry backoff change.
- Impact window (tentative): 08:12–09:40 PT (we're still validating tail).

Customer-facing options:
A) Opt-in header (recommended): X-Redwood-Region: apac — immediate preference for APAC serving tier. Non-breaking; returns are consistent but may add 120–260ms median latency.
B) Account-level route override: we can flip your account to prefer APAC for the next 2–4 hours — we'll handle the change and revert automatically. Requires confirmation from your side.

I'll keep telemetry pushed to status.redwood.ai and post a post-incident summary once we have full RCA. If Monica and Rishi approve, we can offer a one-time service credit for the impacted window.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head of Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Spike in 503s for US-East + EU-Central — are there opt-in fallbacks?

Hi Sophie — quick operational guidance to opt in (two options):

Client-side (fastest):
- Add header: X-Redwood-Region: apac
- Example curl: 
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -H "X-Redwood-Region: apac" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Start with 5–10% of traffic to confirm behaviour, then increase.

Account-level (we manage):
- Reply to this email "Please opt-in Acme to APAC" and we'll shift routing weights for your account immediately. We will monitor and automatically revert when provider peering is healthy.

We will also issue a one-time credit for the impacted window once we confirm exact exposure; I'll coordinate with Monica for credits and documentation. Attached checklist has step-by-step instructions.

Would you like us to opt you in on our side or prefer the client header test first?

— Rishi

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Zhang <sophie@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps — US-East + EU-Central reachability event

Hi Sophie,

Thanks again for the patience while we investigated. Below is a concise post-incident summary and actionable next steps.

Summary of impact
- Date/time window: 2026-04-18 08:12–09:40 PT (primary impact), with residual latencies through 10:15 PT as nodes recovered.
- Affected regions: US-East and EU-Central. APAC serving tier remained healthy.
- Customer exposure: Acme Analytics reported increased 503s and timeouts (we confirmed matching telemetry).

Root cause
- Upstream peering instability between two major transit providers led to packet loss to specific POPs that host our US-East and EU-Central execution nodes. This was a provider-level networking degradation — not an application bug in our runtime.

Actions taken
- Drained and quarantined impacted instances to stop retry storms.
- Increased fallback routing weights toward APAC pool for affected customers (temporary).
- Pushed a retry/backoff change to reduce client-visible 503s.
- Notified customers and provided the opt-in header (X-Redwood-Region: apac) and an account-level override option.

Customer options completed
- Per your confirmation (reply received), we applied the account-level override for Acme at 09:00 PT on 2026-04-18; traffic shifted toward APAC for the duration of the incident.

Credits and follow-up
- We will apply a one-time credit equal to 10% of billable tokens for the impacted window. Monica will follow up with a billing adjustment record within 3 business days.

Preventive work (next 30 days)
- Add more aggressive multi-provider peering checks and automated reweighting for CONN loss exceeding 0.5% within 1m windows.
- Expand our regional canary to detect peering flaps earlier and trigger automated account-level opt-ins when configured.
- Customer-facing: add an "auto-fallback" opt-in toggle in Console for accounts that prefer hands-off rerouting.

References
- Incident timeline & logs: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20260418
- Postmortem doc (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodPostmortem

If you'd like, we can keep Acme auto-opted into APAC for the next 72 hours while the provider mitigations complete. Otherwise we'll revert routing to normal by 04-21 09:00 PT. Please reply with your preference.

Sincere apologies for the disruption — we'll be in touch with the finalized RCA once the internal follow-up items are complete.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
